key_insight: Ground-state energy accuracy and phonon spectra help predict whether pretrained force fields reproduce zirconia’s monoclinic–tetragonal–cubic phase sequence.
engineering_relevance: These diagnostics offer practical screening criteria for selecting lower-cost force fields for finite-temperature phase-transition simulations.
method: Benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for ZrO2.
Compare polymorph energetics and phonon dispersions with matched density functional theory references.
Test phase evolution using variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: Four of ten models reproduced the correct phase sequence; orthorhombic–tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom accompanied spurious intermediates, while ORB models showed 30–60% phonon-frequency compression and unstable variable-cell dynamics.
watch_item: The proposed screening criteria—relative polymorph energies within about 6 meV/atom of matched DFT and no systematic phonon softening—were evaluated on zirconia; transferability to other materials remains unestablished.
paper_title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
